why: Group prices by city in a hash map, then sort each city's list and read the middle. All prices are known up front, so a plain sort per city is simpler than the streaming two-heap median, which only pays off when queries interleave with inserts.
hints: Each city is independent: first collect its prices.
Use a dict city -> list of prices; sort each list once and take the middle element (odd) or average the two middles (even).
Output cities in sorted order as 'city=median', printing an integer when the median is whole and 'x.5' otherwise. O(N log N) overall.
pitfalls: Format matters: 6 not 6.0, and 1.5 for a half; compute with integers (sum of the two middles, then check parity).
Cities must be sorted by name in the output, not by first appearance.
statement:
Each entry is a string "city price" (city has no spaces, price is a non-negative integer). For every city, find the median of its prices: the middle value after sorting, or the mean of the two middle values when the count is even. Return one string "city=median" per city, sorted by city name. Write the median as an integer when it is whole, otherwise with a .5 suffix.

Worked example: ["sf 10","ny 4","sf 20","ny 8","sf 30"]

  • ny prices sorted: [4, 8]; even count, median = (4 + 8) / 2 = 6, written 6.
  • sf prices sorted: [10, 20, 30]; median = 20.
  • Sort by city: ny, sf.

Answer: ["ny=6","sf=20"]. For ["a 1","a 2"] the median is 1.5, giving ["a=1.5"].
